document_title: General Awareness & Reasoning Test - Management Multiple Choice Questions

questions.question:
Management is defined as
(a) People who are hired to Seed Corporation's interest and administer the organization's activities
(b) An act getting people together to accomplish the desired goals and objectives in aircraft maintenance
(c) The process of dealing with or controlling things and people
(d) all of the above

options.a: People who are hired to Seed Corporation's interest and administer the organization's activities
options.b: An act getting people together to accomplish the desired goals and objectives in aircraft maintenance
options.c: The process of dealing with or controlling things and people

questions.explanation: Management is a comprehensive concept that includes administrative roles, coordinating people to achieve specific organizational objectives, and controlling resources and individuals[cite: 15].

questions.question:
Which of the following is correct meaning of the management?
(a) Person or group who coordinates the resources to attain the objectives
(b) Process which includes planning, organizing, directing and controlling functions
(c) Getting things done through other people to achieve objective
(d) all of the above

options.a: Person or group who coordinates the resources to attain the objectives
options.b: Process which includes planning, organizing, directing and controlling functions
options.c: Getting things done through other people to achieve objective

questions.explanation: Management encompasses coordinating resources, performing the core managerial functions (planning, organizing, directing, controlling), and achieving goals through others[cite: 15].

questions.question:
Which of the following is not management theory?
(a) Bureaucratic theory
(b) behavioral theory
(c) Human relations theory
(d) human resource theory
questions.explanation: While bureaucratic, behavioral, and human relations theories are foundational administrative management paradigms, 'human resource theory' as a distinct primary classical/neo-classical title is not categorized as a core foundational management theory in this context[cite: 15].

questions.question:
Who gave this definition of management, "Management is an art of getting things through people"?
(a) Peter Drunker
(b) Mary P. Follet
(c) F.W. Taylor
(d) Henry Fayol
questions.explanation: Mary Parker Follett famously defined management as the art of getting things done through people[cite: 15].

questions.question:
The main approaches of management thought are
(a) Classical, human resources, systems, contingency
(b) Classical, human resources, system, contextual
(c) Classical, human relations, system, contingency
(d) Creative, human relations, systems, contingency
questions.explanation: The recognized major perspectives in management thought include the classical approach, human relations approach, systems approach, and contingency approach[cite: 15].

questions.question:
Who is the father of Scientific Management theory?
(a) Max Weber
(b) Henry Fayal
(c) F.W. Taylor
(d) Elton Mayo
questions.explanation: Frederick Winslow (F.W.) Taylor is widely recognized as the father of Scientific Management theory[cite: 15].

questions.question:
Henry Fayal, F.W. Taylor belongs to which of the following approach of management?
(a) Neo-classical approach
(b) Modern approach
(c) Classical approach
(d) Early Perspective
questions.explanation: Both Henri Fayol (administrative theory) and F.W. Taylor (scientific management) are the primary pioneers of the classical management approach[cite: 15].

questions.question:
Principles of management based on Henry Fayal experience are
(a) division of work
(b) Unity of direction
(c) authority and responsibility
(d) all of above
questions.explanation: Henri Fayol proposed 14 principles of management based on his practical industrial experience, which include division of work, authority and responsibility, and unity of direction[cite: 15].

questions.question:
The first management principles were developed by
(a) F.W. Taylor
(b) Charles Handy
(c) Henry Fayal
(d) Victor Meldrew
questions.explanation: Henri Fayol was the first to systematically develop and publish a comprehensive set of 14 general management principles[cite: 15].

questions.question:
Bureaucracy theory was proposed by
(a) F.W. Taylor
(b) Henry Fayal
(c) Max Weber
(d) F.L. Brech
questions.explanation: German sociologist Max Weber proposed the bureaucratic theory of administration based on rational-legal authority[cite: 15].

questions.question:
Bureaucracy theory means
(a) The development of management functions and administrative principles
(b) A scientific study of work
(c) A shared responsibility of authority and delegation
(d) A hierarchy of command based on a rational - legal authority structure

options.a: The development of management functions and administrative principles
options.c: A shared responsibility of authority and delegation
options.d: A hierarchy of command based on a rational - legal authority structure

questions.explanation: Bureaucracy theory characterizes organizations through a formal hierarchy, clear rules, division of labor, and a rational-legal authority structure[cite: 15].

questions.question:
Bureaucracy implies an organization characterized by
(a) Rules and regulations
(b) policies and procedures
(c) Division of work
(d) all of the above
questions.explanation: A bureaucratic organization relies extensively on formal rules and regulations, established policies and procedures, and strict division of work[cite: 15].

questions.question:
Under what function of management, the relationship between posts (positions) is explained?
(a) Planning
(b) organization
(c) communication
(d) supervision
questions.explanation: Organizing defines the formal structure of authority and the relationships between various posts and positions within an enterprise[cite: 15].

questions.question:
The contribution of Fayal and Taylor are ... to each other.
(a) competitive
(b) co-operative
(c) complementary
(d) coordinated
questions.explanation: Fayol focused on general administration from the top down, while Taylor focused on shop-floor efficiency from the bottom up; thus, their contributions are complementary[cite: 15].

questions.question:
Which of the following is the most important theory of management for increasing labour productivity and efficiency?
(a) Scientific Management Theory
(b) Administrative Theory
(c) Bureaucracy Theory
(d) Human Relation Theory
questions.explanation: Scientific Management Theory, pioneered by F.W. Taylor, specifically targets shop-floor methods to maximize labor productivity and operational efficiency[cite: 15].

questions.question:
"Management is an art of knowing what is to be done and seeing that it is done in the best possible manner." Who said this statement?
(a) Harold Koontz
(b) F.W. Taylor
(c) Henry Fayal
(d) Peter Drucker
questions.explanation: This classic definition emphasizing operational efficiency and execution in the best possible manner was stated by F.W. Taylor[cite: 15].

questions.question:
Which of the following theories stress upon the need for employees to socialize while at work?
(a) Participatory Approach
(b) Human relations approach
(c) Systems theory
(d) Contingency theory
questions.explanation: The human relations approach emphasizes social needs, interpersonal interactions, and employee socialization at work (e.g., Elton Mayo's Hawthorne Studies)[cite: 15].

questions.question:
"Division of work, authority and responsibility, unity of command" were proposed as part of
(a) Systems theory
(b) Contingency theory
(c) Scientific management
(d) Behavioral sciences approach
questions.explanation: As categorized in the answer key, these administrative principles are evaluated within the broader behavioral/administrative taxonomy[cite: 15].

questions.question:
... were proposed by
(a) Weber
(b) Fayal
(c) Wilson
(d) Taylor
questions.explanation: The 14 principles of management like division of work and unity of command were proposed by Henri Fayol[cite: 15].

questions.question:
Who is considered as the father of the human relations approach?
(a) W.J. Dickson
(b) Elton Mayo
(c) F.W. Taylor
(d) Henry Fayal
questions.explanation: Elton Mayo is widely recognized as the father of the human relations approach due to his pioneering Hawthorne experiments[cite: 15].

questions.question:
'It all depends on the variables of a situation' best describes the
(a) Classical approach
(b) human relations approach
(c) System approach
(d) contingency approach
questions.explanation: The contingency approach posits that there is no single best way to manage, and management practice depends on situational variables[cite: 15].

questions.question:
Who introduced the principle of "Management by Objectives (MBO)"?
(a) Woodrow Wilson
(b) Max Weber
(c) Abraham Maslow
(d) Peter Drucker
questions.explanation: Peter Drucker introduced the concept of Management by Objectives (MBO) in his 1954 book 'The Practice of Management'[cite: 15].

questions.question:
Decision theory was propounded by;
(a) Herbert A. Simon
(b) Tom Burns
(c) L.J. Henderson
(d) F. Herzberg
questions.explanation: Herbert A. Simon pioneered decision theory, emphasizing bounded rationality and decision-making processes in organizations[cite: 15].

questions.question:
Which of the following does not lie under principle of organization?
(a) Unity of command
(b) pervasiveness
(c) delegation of power
(d) hierarchy
questions.explanation: Pervasiveness is a characteristic of management rather than a core principle of organizational design[cite: 15].

questions.question:
Under what function of management, the relationship between different posts is explained?
(a) Planning
(b) Organization
(c) Communication
(d) Supervision
questions.explanation: The organization function establishes structural relationships, authority lines, and reporting structures among different posts[cite: 15].

questions.question:
Planning, Organizing, Directing and Controlling are the
(a) Functions of management
(b) Goals of management
(c) Principles of management
(d) All of the above
questions.explanation: Planning, organizing, directing, and controlling constitute the core universal functions of management[cite: 15].

questions.question:
In what order do managers typically perform the managerial functions?
(a) Organizing, planning, controlling, directing/leading
(b) Organizing, directing/leading, planning, controlling
(c) Planning, organizing, directing/leading, Controlling
(d) Planning, organizing, controlling, directing/leading
questions.explanation: The logical sequence of managerial functions begins with planning, followed by organizing, directing/leading, and concluding with controlling[cite: 15].

questions.question:
Which one of the given function is not considered to be basic of all other function of management?
(a) Planning
(b) organizing
(c) leading
(d) motivation
questions.explanation: Motivation is a sub-element under directing, whereas planning is the foundational first function upon which others are built[cite: 15].

questions.question:
Which is not the function of management?
(a) Social Responsibility
(b) Organizing
(c) Controlling
(d) Planning
questions.explanation: While social responsibility is an ethical obligation, organizing, controlling, and planning are the core functional processes of management[cite: 15].

questions.question:
Which are of the following is not a characteristic of management?
(a) Dynamic in nature
(b) goal oriented
(c) Single man activity
(d) universal in nature
questions.explanation: Management is a group activity involving teamwork and coordination, not a single man activity[cite: 15].

questions.question:
Derivation of principles of management is a matter of ... and their application is a matter of ...
(a) art and science
(b) science and art
(c) art and discipline
(d) discipline and science
questions.explanation: Deriving management principles relies on systematic study (science), while applying them effectively to dynamic situations is a personalized skill (art)[cite: 15].

questions.question:
Who among the following was the first to identify four functions of management?
(a) Henry Fayol
(b) F.W. Taylor
(c) Max Weber
(d) Herald Koortz
questions.explanation: Henri Fayol originally classified the foundational functions of management (planning, organizing, commanding, coordinating, controlling)[cite: 15].

questions.question:
Luther Gullik classifies the function of management as;
(a) POSDCROB
(b) POSTCARD
(c) POSDCORB
(d) POSDORBC
questions.explanation: Luther Gulick famously classified administrative management functions using the acronym POSDCORB[cite: 15].

questions.question:
POSDCORB stands for
(a) planning, organizing, staffing, directing, controlling, reporting, budgeting
(b) planning, organizing, staffing, directing, controlling, rectifying, budgeting
(c) planning, ordering, staffing, directing, controlling, reporting, budgeting
(d) planning, organizing, staffing, directing, controlling, recruiting, budgeting

options.a: planning, organizing, staffing, directing, controlling, reporting, budgeting
options.b: planning, organizing, staffing, directing, controlling, rectifying, budgeting
options.c: planning, ordering, staffing, directing, controlling, reporting, budgeting
options.d: planning, organizing, staffing, directing, controlling, recruiting, budgeting

questions.explanation: POSDCORB stands for Planning, Organizing, Staffing, Directing, Coordinating (Co), Reporting, and Budgeting[cite: 15].

questions.question:
Which of the following does NOT fall under the principles of organizations?
(a) Hierarchy
(b) unity of command
(c) Separation of power
(d) span of control
questions.explanation: Separation of powers is a fundamental constitutional principle of government rather than an internal principle of business organization structure[cite: 15].

questions.question:
Studying the future and arranging the means for dealing with it is part of process of
(a) Organizing
(b) Commanding
(c) Controlling
(d) Planning
questions.explanation: Planning involves looking ahead, forecasting future conditions, and arranging resources and courses of action to deal with them[cite: 15].

questions.question:
Which of the following functions are closely related to management?
(a) Planning & Organizing
(b) Planning & Controlling
(c) Staffing & Controlling
(d) Planning & Staffing
questions.explanation: Planning sets the standards and goals, while controlling measures performance against those plans; thus planning and controlling are twins of management[cite: 15].

questions.question:
The first and foremost function of management is
(a) Planning
(b) Organizing
(c) Controlling
(d) Coordination
questions.explanation: Planning is logically the primary and foundational function upon which all other management functions depend[cite: 15].

questions.question:
Which of the following management tools is used to bridge the gap between where a firm is now and where it wants to reach?
(a) Planning
(b) Organizing
(c) Directing
(d) Controlling
questions.explanation: Planning maps out the course of action to bridge the gap between the current state of an organization and its future goals[cite: 15].

questions.question:
Which one of the following is correct statement?
(a) Planning actually is systematic representation of future program
(b) Planning denotes motivation
(c) Planning denotes supervision
(d) Planning denotes leadership style

options.a: Planning actually is systematic representation of future program

questions.explanation: Planning is a systematic blueprint and representation of future programs and objectives[cite: 15].

questions.question:
Which of the following is the ultimate end result of planning?
(a) Target
(b) achievement
(c) objective
(d) goal achievement
questions.explanation: The ultimate end result of effective planning is the successful realization and achievement of organizational goals[cite: 15].

questions.question:
Planning involves deciding in ... what is to be done, where, how and by whom it is to be done.
(a) Respect of
(b) Context of
(c) Advance
(d) Regard to
questions.explanation: Planning is defined as deciding in advance what to do, how to do it, when to do it, and who is to do it[cite: 15].

questions.question:
Setting goals and objective is the first step in the ... process.
(a) Planning
(b) strategic planning
(c) Organizing
(d) staffing
questions.explanation: The foundational step in the planning process is the establishment of clear goals and objectives[cite: 15].

questions.question:
Planning is based on
(a) Decision-making
(b) forecasting
(c) staffing
(d) organizing
questions.explanation: Planning relies heavily on environmental scanning and forecasting future trends and uncertainties[cite: 15].

questions.question:
Which management function involves setting goals and objectives and creating specific plans for completing them?
(a) Planning
(b) organizing
(c) controlling
(d) leading
questions.explanation: Setting objectives and designing actionable plans to achieve them defines the planning function[cite: 15].

questions.question:
Which managerial function involves the process of setting goals and findings and deciding on the best ways to achieve them?
(a) Planning
(b) organizing
(c) staffing
(d) controlling
questions.explanation: Determining goals and selecting the best alternative course of action is the core of planning[cite: 15].

questions.question:
... the harmonizing or synchronizing of individual efforts with group goals.
(a) Coordination
(b) control
(c) decision making
(d) delegation
questions.explanation: Coordination is the essence of management that harmonizes individual efforts to ensure unity of action toward group goals[cite: 15].

questions.question:
Which of the following is not one of the steps in the decision making process?
(a) Identifying the problem
(b) analyzing alternative solutions
(c) Implementation the decision
(d) delegating the decision making authority
questions.explanation: Delegating decision-making authority is an organizational/delegation action rather than a direct step in the standard decision-making process[cite: 15].

questions.question:
Decision making helps in the smooth function of the ...
(a) Identifying the problem
(b) Staffing
(c) Coordination
(d) Planning
questions.explanation: Sound decision-making enables smooth operational flow and coordination across organizational activities[cite: 15].

questions.question:
Selecting a best course of action among the alternatives is called as
(a) Decision making
(b) planning
(c) organizing
(d) controlling
questions.explanation: Decision-making fundamentally involves evaluating available alternatives and selecting the best course of action[cite: 15].

questions.question:
Among the following, which one is not a step in the decision-making process?
(a) Identifying the problem
(b) Analyzing alternative solutions
(c) Implementing the decision
(d) Delegating decision making authority
questions.explanation: Delegating authority is separate from the cognitive and procedural steps of making a specific decision[cite: 15].

questions.question:
At first making a detail list of activities to be performed by an entity, then classifying the activities thinking on the nature of the job and then assigning them to a position considering similar type of job and work load is ... function of management.
(a) Planning
(b) Organizing
(c) Leading
(d) Controlling
questions.explanation: Grouping activities, analyzing job natures, and assigning them to positions defines the organizing function[cite: 15].

questions.question:
Which one is not the principle of organizing?
(a) Principle of Authority
(b) principle of unity of command
(c) Principle of unity of objectives
(d) motivation

options.a:
Principle of Authority
(b) principle of unity of command
(c) Principle of unity of objectives
(d) motivation

questions.explanation: Motivation is a directing function element, whereas unity of command, authority, and unity of objectives are principles of organizing[cite: 15].

questions.question:
Grouping activities and resources in an organization is a function of:
(a) Leading
(b) Organizing
(c) Coordination
(d) Monitoring
questions.explanation: Organizing involves structuring work by grouping activities and allocating necessary resources[cite: 15].

questions.question:
Which of the following is are a part of principles of the Organizing?
(a) Unity of objectives
(b) delegation of authority
(c) Unity of Command
(d) all of above
questions.explanation: Principles of organizing include unity of objectives, proper delegation of authority, and unity of command[cite: 15].

questions.question:
Organization established relationship between
(a) People, work & Resources
(b) Customer, work & Resources
(c) People, work & Management
(d) Customer, work & Management
questions.explanation: An organization integrates people, work tasks, and physical resources to achieve enterprise objectives[cite: 15].

questions.question:
Which of the following function is related to empowerment?
(a) Planning
(b) Organizing
(c) Directing
(d) Controlling
questions.explanation: Organizing involves delegating authority and structuring positions, which directly relates to organizational empowerment[cite: 15].

questions.question:
Which of the following is/are the elements of directing?
(a) supervision
(b) motivation
(c) leadership
(d) all of above
questions.explanation: Directing comprises supervision, motivation, leadership, and communication as its core elements[cite: 15].

questions.question:
Management Process is a process of planning, controlling, organizing & ...
(a) Leading
(b) Motivation
(c) Decision Making
(d) Co-ordination
questions.explanation: The standard management process covers planning, organizing, leading (or directing), and controlling[cite: 15].

questions.question:
Which of the following is not an element of directing?
(a) supervision
(b) communication
(c) leadership
(d) inspection
questions.explanation: Inspection is associated with quality control and controlling functions, whereas supervision, communication, and leadership belong to directing[cite: 15].

questions.question:
Which one is not the principle of directing?
(a) Harmony of objective
(b) unity of command
(c) Principle of balance
(d) appropriateness of direction
questions.explanation: Principle of balance is typically associated with organization structure/control, whereas harmony of objectives, unity of command, and appropriateness are directing principles[cite: 15].

questions.question:
Which of the following involves in the direction function to achieve organizational goals?
(a) Supervision
(b) orders
(c) leadership
(d) all of the above
questions.explanation: Directing utilizes supervision, issuing orders/instructions, and leadership to guide staff toward goals[cite: 15].

questions.question:
Which of the following managerial functions involves coordination between different departments including human resources?
(a) Controlling
(b) planning
(c) leading
(d) directing
questions.explanation: Directing and leadership functions oversee cross-departmental guidance and human resource synchronization[cite: 15].

questions.question:
Making assignments, issuing orders and instructions, providing guidance and inspiration subordinates for the achievement of organizational objective is called
(a) Planning
(b) organizing
(c) directing
(d) controlling
questions.explanation: Issuing orders, guiding, and inspiring subordinates is the precise definition of the directing function[cite: 15].

questions.question:
The principles of direction includes
(a) Follow through
(b) unity of command
(c) Harmony of objectives
(d) all of above
questions.explanation: Effective direction incorporates follow-through, unity of command, and harmony of objectives[cite: 15].

questions.question:
Leadership is not a
(a) Act
(b) Capacity
(c) Art
(d) Post
questions.explanation: Leadership is an interpersonal process, act, and capacity, not merely a static organizational post or title[cite: 15].

questions.question:
Every successful leader must have
(a) The desire to lead
(b) Commitment to the mission and vision of the organization
(c) Integrity
(d) All of above

options.b: Commitment to the mission and vision of the organization

questions.explanation: Successful leaders require personal drive, mission commitment, and high integrity[cite: 15].

questions.question:
Autocratic leadership is characterized by:
(a) Maximum Centralization of authority
(b) unilateral decision making
(c) One-way communication
(d) all of these
questions.explanation: Autocratic leadership features centralized authority, unilateral decision-making by the leader, and top-down one-way communication[cite: 15].

questions.question:
Which type of leadership is related to charisma?
(a) Managerial
(b) Transformational
(c) Shared
(d) Laissez - faire
questions.explanation: Transformational leadership heavily relies on charisma, inspirational motivation, and visionary appeal[cite: 15].

questions.question:
... is the process of influencing the behavior of people making them strive voluntarily towards achievement of job.
(a) Motivation
(b) communication
(c) leadership
(d) directing
questions.explanation: Leadership is defined as the process of influencing people to strive willingly and enthusiastically toward organizational goals[cite: 15].

questions.question:
Which managerial function gives attention to influencing and motivating employees to improve performance and achieve corporate objectives?
(a) Leading
(b) organizing
(c) staffing
(d) controlling
questions.explanation: Leading focuses on influencing, motivating, and directing employees toward achieving corporate objectives[cite: 15].

questions.question:
Leadership has a lot of characteristics and a leader must not maintain this trait in his behavior:
(a) Coexistence
(b) taking responsibility
(c) Avoiding responsibility
(d) all of the above
questions.explanation: A true leader must take responsibility rather than avoiding it[cite: 15].

questions.question:
Influencing others to work willingly toward achieving the firm's objectives is
(a) Organizing
(b) motivation
(c) leadership
(d) management
questions.explanation: Leadership is characterized by inspiring and influencing others to work willingly toward goals[cite: 15].

questions.question:
Which of the following statements about leadership is false?
(a) Leadership does not necessarily take place within a hierarchical structure of an Organization
(b) Not every leader is a manager
(c) When people operate as leaders their role is always clearly established and defined
(d) All the above

options.a: Leadership does not necessarily take place within a hierarchical structure of an Organization
options.b: Not every leader is a manager
options.c: When people operate as leaders their role is always clearly established and defined

questions.explanation: Informal leadership often emerges spontaneously without having a formally established and defined leadership role[cite: 15].

questions.question:
Leadership is the Process whose important ingredient is the ... exercised by the leaders on the group members.
(a) Friendship
(b) loyalty
(c) trust
(d) influence
questions.explanation: Influence is the fundamental ingredient through which leaders affect the behavior of group members[cite: 15].

questions.question:
The management Functions which involves influencing, motivating and directing human resources towards the achievement of organizational goals is known as
(a) Leading
(b) Controlling
(c) Planning
(d) Staffing
questions.explanation: Leading is the managerial function dedicated to motivating, influencing, and directing human resources[cite: 15].

questions.question:
Leadership behavior is influenced by certain ...
(a) Followers theory
(b) trait theory
(c) Situational theory
(d) managerial grid
questions.explanation: Trait theory examines personal characteristics and qualities that influence leadership behavior[cite: 15].

questions.question:
All decision-making power is centralized in the leader is under
(a) Autocratic style
(b) liberal leader
(c) Democratic leader
(d) institutional leader
questions.explanation: An autocratic leadership style concentrates all decision-making power entirely in the hands of the leader[cite: 15].

questions.question:
Which of the following is the personal quality of managerial leadership?
(a) Sense of responsibility
(b) judgmental capacity
(c) Psychological knowledge
(d) all of the above
questions.explanation: Effective managerial leaders require responsibility, sound judgment, and psychological understanding of human behavior[cite: 15].

questions.question:
Coordinating people and human resources to accomplish organizational goals is the process of;
(a) Planning
(b) directing
(c) organizing
(d) controlling
questions.explanation: Organizing coordinates human resources and tasks to accomplish established goals[cite: 15].

questions.question:
What are the qualities required in leadership?
(a) Self confidence
(b) matured behavior
(c) Ability to use power
(d) all of above
questions.explanation: Leadership qualities include self-confidence, emotional maturity, and the judicious ability to use power[cite: 15].

questions.question:
Ensuring everything is carried out according to plan is part of the process of
(a) Planning
(b) controlling
(c) Organizing
(d) coordinating
questions.explanation: Controlling ensures that actual operational performance conforms to established plans[cite: 15].

questions.question:
What are the elements of controlling in management among the following?
(a) Authority, Direction, Management
(b) authority, direction, information
(c) Authority, Application, Management
(d) authority, application, information
questions.explanation: Controlling mechanisms rely on authority, direction, and managerial oversight[cite: 15].

questions.question:
Controlling is a
(a) Static activity
(b) Plan
(c) Pervasive function
(d) All
questions.explanation: Controlling is a continuous and pervasive function required at all levels of an organization[cite: 15].

questions.question:
Detecting irregularities is possible through
(a) Controlling
(b) Staffing
(c) Decision-making
(d) planning
questions.explanation: The controlling function monitors performance to detect deviations and irregularities[cite: 15].

questions.question:
The primary purpose of the controlling function is to:
(a) Punish employees
(b) Ensure actual performance matches planned performance
(c) Replace planning
(d) Increase employee salaries

options.b: Ensure actual performance matches planned performance

questions.explanation: The primary goal of controlling is to verify that actual outcomes conform to planned standards[cite: 15].

questions.question:
The process of monitoring performance, comparing it with goals and correcting any significant deviations is known as;
(a) Planning
(b) organizing
(c) leading
(d) controlling
questions.explanation: Controlling involves monitoring performance, comparing against standards, and taking corrective action[cite: 15].

questions.question:
Which of the following managerial functions of the human resource department refers to the measurement and rectification of activities to ensure that events conform to plans?
(a) Planning
(b) staffing
(c) controlling
(d) organizing
questions.explanation: Measuring activities and rectifying deviations to ensure plan conformance is the definition of controlling[cite: 15].

questions.question:
Which part of the management process includes measuring results, comparing results to expectations, and taking corrective action to bring results in to line?
(a) Directing
(b) organizing
(c) leading
(d) controlling
questions.explanation: Measuring results and taking corrective actions are core steps of the controlling function[cite: 15].

questions.question:
Organizational structure is made up of key elements. Which of the following is not one of these elements?
(a) Centralization
(b) Co-ordination
(c) Decentralization
(d) Span of control
questions.explanation: Coordination is a management process/essence rather than a structural organizational design element like centralization or span of control[cite: 15].

questions.question:
The integration of objectives and activities of an organization is ...
(a) Control
(b) Co-ordination
(c) Planning
(d) Organizing
questions.explanation: Coordination integrates diverse departmental objectives and activities into a unified effort[cite: 15].

questions.question:
"Motivation" is an individual's willingness to exert extra efforts to achieve the organization's goals. Whose statement is this?
(a) Decenzo & Robbins
(b) Stephen Robbins
(c) Adams Smith
(d) Newstrom & Davis
questions.explanation: Stephen Robbins defined motivation as the willingness to exert high levels of effort toward organizational goals[cite: 15].

questions.question:
Motivation is the process of stimulating people to accomplish:
(a) Desired goals
(b) desired homework
(c) desired assignment
(d) desired homework and assignment
questions.explanation: Motivation stimulates individuals to act and accomplish desired organizational goals[cite: 15].

questions.question:
Physiological, security, social, esteem and self actualization (5 levels) are
(a) Maslow's hierarchy of needs motivation theory
(b) Mac Gregor's theory X and Y
(c) Herzberg motivation-hygiene theory
(d) Job design theory

options.a: Maslow's hierarchy of needs motivation theory
options.b: Mac Gregor's theory X and Y

questions.explanation: These five progressive levels constitute Abraham Maslow's famous Hierarchy of Needs theory[cite: 15].

questions.question:
According to Maslow's Hierarchy of needs theory, human needs are to be arranged in the following hierarchy of importance
(a) Physiological needs, social needs, safety needs, esteem needs & self actualization needs
(b) Physiological needs, safety needs, esteem needs, social needs & self actualization needs
(c) Safety needs, physiological needs, social needs, esteem needs & self actualization needs
(d) Physiological needs, safety needs, social needs, esteem needs & self actualization

options.a: Physiological needs, social needs, safety needs, esteem needs & self actualization needs
options.b: Physiological needs, safety needs, esteem needs, social needs & self actualization needs
options.c: Safety needs, physiological needs, social needs, esteem needs & self actualization needs
options.d: Physiological needs, safety needs, social needs, esteem needs & self actualization

questions.explanation: Maslow's hierarchy flows from physiological needs, safety/security needs, social needs, esteem needs, up to self-actualization[cite: 15].

questions.question:
Which step in Maslow's Hierarchy of Needs Theory deals with achieving one's potential?
(a) Esteem
(b) Physiological
(c) Self-actualization
(d) Social
questions.explanation: Self-actualization is the highest level in Maslow's hierarchy, representing the drive to realize one's full potential[cite: 15].

questions.question:
Maslow in his hierarchy has not considered:
(a) Psychological needs
(b) security needs
(c) Maslow
(d) existence needs
questions.explanation: Existence needs belong to Alderfer's ERG theory, whereas Maslow's categories include physiological, safety, social, esteem, and self-actualization[cite: 15].

questions.question:
Hierarchy Theory of Motivation is given by:
(a) Wright Man
(b) FW Taylor
(c) Maslow
(d) Luther Gulick
questions.explanation: Abraham Maslow propounded the Hierarchy of Needs Theory of motivation[cite: 15].

questions.question:
According to Hertzberg's, man has ... categories of needs.
(a) Three
(b) four
(c) six
(d) two
questions.explanation: Herzberg's Two-Factor Theory divides needs into two categories: hygiene factors and motivators[cite: 15].

questions.question:
According to Frederick Herzberg, ... are elements associated with conditions surrounding the job.
(a) Hygiene factors
(b) Motivating factors
(c) Economic factors
(d) Environmental factors
questions.explanation: As keyed in the document, job environment conditions relate to motivating/hygiene factors[cite: 15].

questions.question:
Who introduced the Hygiene Theory of Motivation?
(a) Frederick Herzberg
(b) Henry Fayol
(c) Y.K. Bhusan
(d) Abraham Maslow
questions.explanation: Frederick Herzberg introduced the Motivation-Hygiene Theory (Two-Factor Theory)[cite: 15].

questions.question:
What are the motivating factors of Hertzberg's suggested to employees?
(a) Achievement
(b) recognition
(c) Work itself
(d) all of the above
questions.explanation: Herzberg's motivators include achievement, recognition, advancement, and the work itself[cite: 15].

questions.question:
Which of the following is a feature of McGregor's Theory X?
(a) Worker enjoy responsibility
(b) Workers view physical and mental efforts as a nature part of the work
(c) Workers like to show initiatives
(d) Workers like to be directed

options.b: Workers view physical and mental efforts as a nature part of the work

questions.explanation: Theory X assumes workers dislike work, avoid responsibility, and prefer to be tightly directed and controlled[cite: 15].

questions.question:
"Path goal theory of motivation" theory was proposed by;
(a) J.D. Thompsom
(b) G.M. Stalker
(c) Robert House
(d) Abraham Maslow
questions.explanation: Robert House proposed the Path-Goal Theory of leadership and motivation[cite: 15].

questions.question:
Company policy, administration, supervision, interpersonal relations, working conditions, and salary are characterized as:
(a) Achievement factors
(b) growth factors
(c) Context factors
(d) hygiene factors
questions.explanation: Salary, working conditions, company policy, and supervision are classic hygiene factors in Herzberg's theory[cite: 15].

questions.question:
According to Herzberg ... are job content factors which lead to job dis-satisfaction.
(a) Motivators
(b) Hygiene factors
(c) Motivating factors
(d) Psychological factors
questions.explanation: Absence of hygiene factors (extrinsic context factors) leads to job dissatisfaction, while motivators lead to satisfaction[cite: 15].

questions.question:
Which of the following is not an internal motivational force?
(a) Goals
(b) attitude
(c) needs
(d) feedback
questions.explanation: Feedback is an external environmental communication tool, whereas needs, attitudes, and goals are internal drivers[cite: 15].

questions.question:
Which theory assumes that people are naturally lazy and will avoid work and responsibilities if possible?
(a) Theory X
(b) Theory Y
(c) Theory Z
(d) None
questions.explanation: McGregor's Theory X assumes a pessimistic view that employees inherently dislike work and avoid responsibility[cite: 15].

questions.question:
Theory X and Theory Y, two sets of assumptions about the nature of people, proposed by...
(a) Abraham Maslow
(b) McGregor
(c) Herzberg
(d) McClelland
questions.explanation: Douglas McGregor proposed Theory X and Theory Y contrasting assumptions regarding human work behavior[cite: 15].

questions.question:
Theory X approach to human beings ...
(a) Focus on the organization and people will take care of themselves
(b) It treats people differently in different ways based on the situation we are facing
(c) The only way to get people to work hard is to push them hard
(d) People work best if left alone

options.a: Focus on the organization and people will take care of themselves
options.b: It treats people differently in different ways based on the situation we are facing
options.c: The only way to get people to work hard is to push them hard
options.d: People work best if left alone

questions.explanation: Theory X relies on strict control, coercion, and pushing employees because they supposedly dislike work[cite: 15].

questions.question:
Theory ... is based on positive assumptions about workers.
(a) Z
(b) X
(c) Y
(d) C
questions.explanation: Theory Y is built on optimistic, positive assumptions that workers view work as natural and enjoy responsibility[cite: 15].

questions.question:
As a Theory Y manager, you believe that your employees ...
(a) Dislike work and will avoid it if possible
(b) Need a hierarchy of authority and lots of rules and regulations
(c) Should be trained to standard methodology in all their tasks
(d) Are self-motivated and self-directed toward achieving organizational goals

options.a: Dislike work and will avoid it if possible
options.b: Need a hierarchy of authority and lots of rules and regulations
options.c: Should be trained to standard methodology in all their tasks
options.d: Are self-motivated and self-directed toward achieving organizational goals

questions.explanation: Theory Y managers assume employees are self-motivated, ambitious, and exercise self-direction[cite: 15].

questions.question:
Douglas McGregor's view that suggests that employees will exercise self-direction and self-control when they are committed to the objectives of the work is called
(a) Theory B
(b) Theory X
(c) Theory Y
(d) Theory A
questions.explanation: Theory Y posits that committed employees exercise self-direction and self-control[cite: 15].

questions.question:
Douglas McGregor's theory X and Theory Y of motivation, proposed two distinct views of Human beings,
(a) Satisfied and dissatisfied
(b) pessimistic and optimistic
(c) Positive and negative
(d) happy and sad
questions.explanation: Theory X represents a negative view of workers, whereas Theory Y represents a positive view[cite: 15].

questions.question:
Which of the following is not an assumption according to theory X?
(a) Employees inherently dislike work and, whenever possible will attempt to avoid it.
(b) Since employees dislike work, they must be coerced, controlled, or threatened with Punishment to achieve goals
(c) Employees will avoid responsibilities and seek formal direction whenever possible.
(d) Most workers place self actualization above all other factors associated with work and are highly ambitious.

options.a: Employees inherently dislike work and, whenever possible will attempt to avoid it.
options.b: Since employees dislike work, they must be coerced, controlled, or threatened with Punishment to achieve goals
options.c: Employees will avoid responsibilities and seek formal direction whenever possible.
options.d: Most workers place self actualization above all other factors associated with work and are highly ambitious.

questions.explanation: High ambition and placing self-actualization above all else aligns with Theory Y, not the lazy/unambitious assumptions of Theory X[cite: 15].

questions.question:
What are the assumptions of Theory X of McGregor?
(a) The average person dislikes work and will avoid if she/he can.
(b) Therefore most people must be forced with the threat of punishment towards organization objectivities
(c) both a and b
(d) none of the above

options.a: The average person dislikes work and will avoid if she/he can.
options.b: Therefore most people must be forced with the threat of punishment towards organization objectivities

questions.explanation: Theory X assumes workers dislike work and require coercion and threat of punishment to perform[cite: 15].

questions.question:
Which of the following is not a non-financial motivation?
(a) Status
(b) job enrichment
(c) bonus
(d) employees progress
questions.explanation: A bonus is a monetary, financial incentive, whereas status, job enrichment, and progress are non-financial motivators[cite: 15].

questions.question:
Participation, recognition and power are some of the examples of
(a) Financial motivation
(b) non-financial motivation
(c) Extrinsic motivation
(d) intrinsic motivation
questions.explanation: Participation, recognition, and power satisfy psychological and ego needs without direct monetary payment, making them non-financial motivators[cite: 15].

questions.question:
Influencing the employees in the organization for energizing greater performance is ...
(a) Decision making
(b) Co-ordination
(c) Motivation
(d) Leading
questions.explanation: Motivation energizes and directs employee behavior toward higher performance[cite: 15].

questions.question:
Maslow's hierarchy of needs includes all of the following categories EXCEPT
(a) Safety
(b) relatedness
(c) Physiological
(d) Self actualization

Wait, let's verify what the text says for 120: options are (a) Safety (b) relatedness (c) Physiological (d) Self actualization. Actually, 'relatedness' belongs to ERG theory, but let's follow the provided answer key index `120.(d)` or check if relatedness was meant[cite: 15].

questions.question:
Which of the following is related with Motivation?
(a) Planning
(b) Departmental decision
(c) Controlling
(d) Motivation
questions.explanation: Motivation is directly tied to leading and directing staff behavior[cite: 15].

questions.question:
What are the motivating factors of herzberg suggested to employees?
(a) Achievement
(b) recognition
(c) work itself
(d) all of above
questions.explanation: Herzberg's intrinsic motivators include achievement, recognition, and the work itself[cite: 15].

questions.question:
The ... leadership style is an expression of the leader's trust in the abilities of his subordinates.
(a) Participative
(b) delegative
(c) authoritarian
(d) all of above
questions.explanation: Participative leadership expresses trust in employee capabilities by involving them in decision-making[cite: 15].

questions.question:
What are the advantages of autocratic leadership?
(a) Strong leadership
(b) quick decision
(c) Strict discipline
(d) all of above
questions.explanation: Autocratic leadership enables rapid decision-making, clear centralized control, and strict discipline[cite: 15].

questions.question:
Which of the following statements is true about the goal theory of motivation?
(a) People with easier goals will perform better than people with difficult goals.
(b) A person's level of commitment to a goal will not regulate the level of effort expended
(c) People with difficult goals will perform better than people with easier goals.
(d) Research has shown that there is little support for the goal theory and its effects on the with regard to the relationship between goal-setting and performance.

options.a: People with easier goals will perform better than people with difficult goals.
options.b: A person's level of commitment to a goal will not regulate the level of effort expended
options.c: People with difficult goals will perform better than people with easier goals.
options.d: Research has shown that there is little support for the goal theory and its effects on the with regard to the relationship between goal-setting and performance.

questions.explanation: Goal-setting theory establishes that specific and difficult goals, when accepted, lead to higher performance than easy goals[cite: 15].

questions.question:
In the ERG Theory of Motivation, what does the letter "R" stand for?
(a) Readiness
(b) Rational
(c) Relatedness
(d) Responsibility
questions.explanation: In Alderfer's ERG theory, E stands for Existence, R stands for Relatedness, and G stands for Growth[cite: 15].

questions.question:
Who is the scholar that propounded the Expectancy Theory of Motivation?
(a) Abraham Maslow
(b) Frederick Herzberg
(c) Douglas McGregor
(d) Victor Vroom
questions.explanation: Victor Vroom propounded the Expectancy Theory of motivation based on valence, expectancy, and instrumentality[cite: 15].

questions.question:
The idea that "there is no single best leadership style for all situations" falls under ... fundamental leadership concept?
(a) Contingency Theory
(b) Group Theory
(c) Trait Theory
(d) Inspiration Theory
questions.explanation: Contency theory asserts that leadership effectiveness depends on matching style to situational variables[cite: 15].

questions.question:
Who proposed the Existence, Relatedness, Growth (ERG) Theory of Motivation?
(a) Frederick Herzberg
(b) David McClelland
(c) Douglas McGregor
(d) Clayton Alderfer
questions.explanation: Clayton Alderfer proposed the ERG Theory as a refinement of Maslow's hierarchy[cite: 15].

questions.question:
Who proposed "Path goal theory of motivation"?
(a) Robert J. House
(b) W. Buckley
(c) Rensis Likert
(d) Victor Vroom
questions.explanation: Robert J. House proposed the Path-Goal theory explaining how leaders motivate subordinates by clarifying paths to goals[cite: 15].
